summary: Added a standard-library loopback dashboard and real SQLite application CRUD with stable IDs, bounded validation, literal search, pagination, captured versions and transactional retained audit.
Preserved failed and conflicting drafts, added explicit current-record loading, confirmed deletion/locking, draft export, and independently reported save/list-refresh outcomes.

Added all-or-nothing legacy JSONL import with retained occurrence receipts, non-resurrecting repeat imports, visible unimported CLI history, database identity checks and non-overwriting SQLite backups.

Hardened bounded profile validation and relative document paths; neutralized the example profile; offline planning preserves unknown answers and leaves consent for manual review; logging and launch failures close browser resources.
Added nine detailed source-grounded learning documents, repeatable verification commands, 43 Python and eight Chromium checks, and two reviewed screenshots.

checks.environment: Python 3.13; PyYAML 6.0.3; pydantic 2.13.4; Python Playwright 1.59.0 with Chromium 148; Node 22.16.0
checks.command: python scripts/verify.py; python scripts/verify_browser.py; node --check applybot/web/app.js

limits: Local personal tracker only: one loopback token, no accounts, tenant ownership, distributed limits or production hosting.
New HTTP creates have no durable idempotency receipt; uncertain timeouts require inspection before retry. Audit stores minimal metadata rather than full prior values.
Original paid provider adapters, model availability, career-site automation and real submissions were not exercised. Personal profile and browser session were not loaded or changed.
No power-loss certification, full accessibility audit, automatic draft merge or graphical import wizard.
